name: When Substitution Is Needed
title: When Substitution Is Needed
description: Substitutions happen for obsolescence, cost, availability, or performance. Each trigger needs the same discipline: the substitute must meet or exceed every requirement the original met.
how_it_works: Classify the trigger (obsolete, cheaper, available, better), then list every requirement the original satisfied. The substitute's job description is that list - nothing less.
key_points: Triggers: obsolescence, cost, availability, performance.
List every requirement the original met.
The substitute must meet or exceed all of them.
Different triggers, same discipline.

name: Tolerance Stack-Up on Substitutes
title: Tolerance Stack-Up on Substitutes
description: A substitute with wider tolerance shifts the worst-case analysis. The circuit that worked with 1% parts may fail with 5% - recalculate the stack-up, don't assume.
how_it_works: Re-run worst-case and statistical tolerance analysis with the substitute's tolerances, checking every affected output. If margins shrink below policy, the substitute fails regardless of nominal values.
key_points: Wider tolerances shift worst-case results.
Re-run tolerance analysis with substitute values.
Margins below policy disqualify the substitute.
Nominals lie; tolerances tell the truth.

name: Rating and Derating Checks
title: Rating and Derating Checks
description: Every component has maximum ratings; good design derates below them. A substitute with lower ratings - or the same ratings in a hotter spot - can violate derating policy.
how_it_works: Compare voltage, current, power, and temperature ratings against your derating policy (e.g., 70% of max), in the actual operating environment. A substitute that forces derating violations is rejected.
key_points: Check ratings against derating policy, not just maxima.
Consider the actual operating environment.
Lower-rated substitutes often violate policy silently.
Derating is the margin that keeps products alive.
requirements: Original component specification; substitute candidate datasheet; affected circuit/system parameters identified.
